descriptor: A secure, logged-in web console on top of the deployed Relay system, so RevOps and research-ops analysts and the engineers who run Relay can submit batches and follow them, decide on items that need a human, resubmit or discard failed jobs, and see Relay's health on one screen, with every action protected by password + authenticator login, recorded in an audit log, and impossible to apply twice.

requirements.statement: Every console page and action must require an authenticated session, and logging in must require both the operator's password and a current authenticator (TOTP) code.
Failed logins must be rate-limited per IP and per account, sessions must expire after 8 hours of inactivity, and session cookies must be HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict.

Every console action (login, logout, batch submit, review decision, resubmit, discard) must be appended to a durable audit log with operator, time, action, target and correlation ID before the action is reported as done.
Every state-changing console request must carry a valid per-session CSRF token from the same origin, and be rejected with 403 otherwise.
Every console action must be idempotent: a double-click, a retried request or the same action from two tabs must never apply it twice.
An analyst must be able to upload a CSV (at most 5,000 rows and 2 MB, one required text column), see row-level validation errors before anything is enqueued, and submit the valid rows as one batch.
For each batch the console must show how many items are done, waiting, waiting for review and failed, refresh without a page reload, and offer the results as a CSV download.

The console must list items waiting for review with the reason, the input text and the model's answer and confidence, and let a reviewer approve it, correct it to another label from the fixed taxonomy, or reject it.
A review decision must resolve the item exactly once: it leaves the review queue, its batch result is updated, and the decision is in the audit log.
The console must list escalated failed jobs with their failure reason and class, and let an engineer resubmit one with its original idempotency key or discard it with a required note.
One overview screen must combine the plain-language status with success rate, p95 latency, queue depth and failed-job trends over the last 24 hours.
All console screens must meet WCAG 2.1 AA, work at 360px phone width without horizontal scrolling, and support light and dark mode.
List screens must render in under 1 second with up to 1,000 items, using pagination.
The console must run inside the existing relay-qn Fly.io app with no new paid service, and the public read-only /status page must stay available without login.
Workers must classify each submitted item against the fixed taxonomy and record its outcome per batch, through a classifier adapter so a real model can replace the stand-in without changes elsewhere.

releases.name: Safe Front Door
releases.goal: Prove nobody can act on Relay without password + authenticator login, and that every action is recorded and can't be applied twice.
releases.demo: Log in with a password and a phone authenticator code, see a protected page, get locked out after repeated bad codes, and show the audit log recording every attempt.

releases.name: Batches In, Results Out
releases.goal: An analyst can upload a CSV, watch the batch finish, and download real per-item results.
releases.demo: Upload a 200-row CSV with two bad rows, see the row errors, submit the rest, watch the progress bars fill, and download the classified results.

releases.name: Humans in the Loop
releases.goal: Items that need a person can be decided in the console, exactly once.
releases.demo: Approve one low-confidence item, correct another to a different taxonomy label, reject a third, then resubmit a failed job and discard another with a note, all visible in the audit log.

releases.name: One Screen, Production Ready
releases.goal: Relay's health on one accessible screen, and the whole console live in production.
releases.demo: Open the overview on a phone in dark mode, read the 24-hour trends, then log in to the live console at relay-qn.fly.dev and submit a batch end to end.

stories.title: Log in to the console with a password and an authenticator code
stories.narrative: As an analyst, I want to log in with my password and an authenticator code, so that nobody else can act on Relay in my name.
acceptance: Given a valid password and current TOTP code, When I log in, Then I get a session and reach the protected console home page
Given a wrong password or code, When I log in, Then I am refused with one generic message that doesn't say which part was wrong
Given 5 failed attempts for an account or IP within 15 minutes, When I try again, Then I am refused until the window passes, even with correct credentials
Trust: no console page or action responds without a valid session (401 for API calls, redirect to login for pages), checked against every /console route
failure_paths: A TOTP code from the previous or next 30-second step is rejected because of phone clock drift (allow exactly +/-1 step, never more)
Session store (Redis) unreachable at login: must refuse to log in, never fall back to an unchecked session
Timing difference between unknown user and wrong password leaks which accounts exist
stories.task_guidance: Port CoreOps's hand-rolled auth (ai-operations-center/mcp-server/src/auth/totp.ts and its scrypt credentials helper) into relay/src/console/auth/, node:crypto only. Operator accounts (username, role analyst|engineer, scrypt hash, TOTP secret) live in Redis, created by an admin script run over `fly ssh console`; sessions in Redis with an 8-hour idle TTL; cookies HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict. Add /console routes to the existing status server; leave /status, /status.json and /health public.

stories.title: Record every console action and make it impossible to forge or repeat
stories.narrative: As an engineer, I want every console action recorded and protected against forgery and double-submission, so that I can always say who did what and nothing happens twice.
acceptance: Given a logged-in operator, When they perform any action, Then an audit entry with operator, time, action, target, outcome and correlation ID is written before the response says it succeeded
Given a state-changing request without a valid CSRF token or from another origin, When it arrives, Then it is rejected with 403 and the rejection is audited
Given the same action submitted twice with the same idempotency key, When the second arrives, Then it returns the first result and changes nothing
Trust: if the audit log can't be written, the action is not performed and the operator is told it failed
failure_paths: Audit write fails after the action already happened (must be impossible: audit first or both in one transaction)
Two tabs submit the same action at the same moment (race on the idempotency check)
Audit log grows without bound in Redis
stories.task_guidance: One `performAction(operator, action, idempotencyKey, fn)` wrapper in relay/src/console/actions.ts that every later story uses: checks CSRF + origin, claims the idempotency key with SET NX (same pattern as RedisIdempotencyStore), writes the audit entry to a capped Redis stream (e.g. 90 days), then runs fn. A read-only /console/audit page lists recent entries.

stories.title: Classify each batch item in the workers and record its result
stories.narrative: As an analyst, I want every item I submit to come back with a real classification and status, so that a batch's results mean something.
acceptance: Given a job with a batch id and input text, When a worker handles it, Then it runs classifyJob against the fixed taxonomy and stores the label, confidence and taxonomy version under that batch
Given a classification below the taxonomy's review threshold, When it is stored, Then the item is marked waiting for review and is in the review queue, not marked done
Given the classifier fails or returns a label outside the taxonomy, When the worker handles it, Then the item is marked failed with the reason, and nothing is stored as a result
Trust: each item's stored result is written once (idempotent per job), and a redelivered job never overwrites or double-counts it
failure_paths: Classifier adapter not configured or its API key missing at startup
Classifier call hangs or rate-limits (timeout, capped retries, then failed, never a stuck worker)
Batch counters drift from the per-item statuses after a worker crash mid-update
stories.task_guidance: Add a classifier adapter interface (stand-in keyword classifier and, if approved, a Claude API adapter selected by env var) and call src/classifyJob.ts from the worker path in src/jobRouter.ts / src/workerLoop.ts. Store per-item results in a Redis hash per batch and derive counts from item statuses rather than separate counters. Depends on the open decision about which classifier to use.

stories.title: Submit a batch by uploading a CSV
stories.narrative: As an analyst, I want to upload a CSV of companies and submit it as one batch, so that I don't need an engineer to start a run.
acceptance: Given a valid CSV with a text column, When I upload it, Then I see a preview with the row count and can submit it as one batch
Given rows that are empty, too long, or a file over 5,000 rows or 2 MB, When I upload it, Then I see which rows are wrong and why, and nothing is enqueued until I confirm the valid rows
Given I press submit twice or refresh, When the batch is submitted, Then it is enqueued exactly once
Trust: the submission is audited with the batch id, row count and operator, and every enqueued job carries the batch id and its own correlation ID
failure_paths: CSV with formula-injection cells (=, +, -, @) that later open in Excel
Upload with a non-UTF-8 encoding or a BOM
Redis fills up mid-enqueue (noeviction): partial batch must be reported, not hidden
stories.task_guidance: Parse CSV in relay/src/console/csv.ts without a new dependency (quoted fields, BOM, CRLF), validate, store the batch record, then enqueue through the existing RedisStreamQueue inside performAction. Neutralise formula-leading cells on output (STORY-105), never execute them.

stories.title: Follow a batch's progress and download its results
stories.narrative: As an analyst, I want to see how my batch is doing and download the results, so that I can hand them on without asking anyone.
acceptance: Given a submitted batch, When I open it, Then I see done, waiting, waiting for review and failed counts that refresh without reloading the page
Given a finished batch, When I download results, Then I get a CSV with one row per item: input, label, confidence, status and taxonomy version
Given a list of more than 1,000 batches or items, When I open it, Then it renders in under a second with pagination
Trust: the counts always equal the per-item statuses (no item counted twice or missing), and downloads are audited
failure_paths: Results CSV opened in Excel executes a formula from an input cell
Batch page polled by many tabs overloads Redis (polling interval and cache)
A batch id from another operator's URL (any logged-in operator may view, but the access is audited)
stories.task_guidance: Batch list and detail pages under /console/batches, progress via a small JSON endpoint polled every few seconds. CSV export streams rows and prefixes formula-leading cells with an apostrophe.

stories.title: Decide on items waiting for review
stories.narrative: As a reviewer, I want to approve, correct or reject items the model wasn't sure about, so that low-confidence answers never reach results unchecked.
acceptance: Given an item waiting for review, When I open it, Then I see the reason, the input text, the model's label and confidence, and the taxonomy's labels to choose from
Given I approve or correct it, When I submit, Then the item's batch result is updated with my label, it leaves the queue, and it counts as done
Given I reject it, When I submit, Then it is recorded as rejected with my note and leaves the queue
Trust: a decision is applied exactly once even if two reviewers act on the same item at the same moment, and only labels from the fixed taxonomy are accepted
failure_paths: Two reviewers decide the same item simultaneously
Taxonomy changed since the item was classified (show and record the version used)
Review stream entry consumed but the result update fails (no item lost or left half-decided)
stories.task_guidance: Read the review stream with peek for the list; apply decisions through performAction with the item's idempotency key, updating the batch result and acking/removing the review entry in one step. Validate corrections against the loaded taxonomy codes.

stories.title: Resubmit or discard failed jobs
stories.narrative: As an engineer, I want to see the failed jobs that need a person and resubmit or discard them, so that nothing sits in the escalation stream forgotten.
acceptance: Given escalated failed jobs, When I open the failed jobs page, Then I see each one's failure reason, class and how long it has waited
Given I resubmit one, When I confirm, Then it is enqueued again with its original idempotency key and leaves the list
Given I discard one, When I confirm with a required note, Then it is recorded as discarded and leaves the list
Trust: only engineers can resubmit or discard (analysts see the page read-only), and every action is audited
failure_paths: Resubmitting a job whose original actually succeeded (idempotency key must stop a duplicate)
Discard without a note, or with a note containing HTML
Escalation stream unreachable while the page is open
stories.task_guidance: Build on src/dlqTriage.ts's escalation stream; reuse RedisStreamQueue.enqueue for resubmission so idempotency keys carry over. Role check in performAction.

stories.title: See Relay's health on one overview screen
stories.narrative: As an analyst, I want one screen that tells me in plain words whether Relay is healthy and how it has trended today, so that I don't need two dashboards and an engineer to read them.
acceptance: Given monitoring data, When I open the overview, Then I see the plain-language status plus 24-hour charts of success rate, p95 latency, queue depth and failed jobs
Given monitoring is unavailable or stale, When I open the overview, Then it says so instead of showing old numbers as current
Given a 360px-wide phone in dark mode, When I open any console screen, Then it is readable, has no horizontal scroll, and passes WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard checks
Trust: the public /status page stays available without login and shows no job content
failure_paths: Charts with gaps after a restart or deploy (show the gap, never interpolate invented data)
Colour-only status indicators unreadable for colour-blind users
History endpoint slow with a week of samples
stories.task_guidance: Combine statusView.ts and the SLO dashboard into /console (home), charts as inline SVG from /metrics/history (no chart library), design tokens for light/dark. Run an accessibility pass (axe or the fixing-accessibility skill) over every console page.

stories.title: Ship the console to production and verify it end to end
stories.narrative: As an engineer, I want the console live on relay-qn with real operator accounts, so that analysts can use it without me.
acceptance: Given a deploy, When deploy.sh runs, Then tests gate it, the smoke check covers the console login page and the public status, and a failure rolls back
Given a real operator account created over fly ssh, When they log in from a phone authenticator, Then they can submit a batch, follow it and download results on the live site
Given the console is live, When an unauthenticated request hits any /console route, Then it is refused
Trust: no new paid service, no secrets in the repo, and operator TOTP secrets never appear in logs or command history
failure_paths: Cookie Secure flag breaks login over Fly's HTTPS termination (check the forwarded protocol)
Admin script prints a TOTP secret into shell history
Deploy during an in-progress batch loses no items (workers finish or reclaim)
stories.task_guidance: Extend scripts/deploy.sh's smoke check and docs/runbooks/DEPLOYMENT.md; add an operator-admin runbook (create, disable, reset MFA). Verify on the live URL with a real phone.
